    <item>
      <title>Nusa-dobbel for Leipzig i Meisterligaen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>
      <pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 22:01:28 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <title>Karoline Grøtting best av alle på sesongåpningens siste dag – skiskytter imponerte</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Norwegian ber 5000 kundar sperre bankkortet etter datainnbrot</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norwegian-ber-5000-kundar-sperre-bankkortet-etter-datainnbrot-1.18085456</link>
      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.
Ein skadeleg kode blei lagt inn på nettsidene til Norwegian, som gjorde at kortdetaljar som blei brukt på nettsida kan ha vore synlege i ein kortare periode måndag.
Selskapet oppdaga datainnbrotet onsdag.
Hendinga er rapportert til Datatilsynet.
I førre veke blei det kjent at 144.000 passasjerar hos Norwegian og Widerøe blei lekka i forbindelse med eit datainnbrot hos ein spansk IT-leverandør.</description>
      <category>Flyselskapet Norwegian</category>
      <category>Dataangrep og hacking</category>

    </item>

Fanny Bay neighbours are asking the province to pause its review of two groundwater licence applications. They want the science reviewed and their concerns heard before water decisions, that could impact their wells, are made.

]]>

Fanny Bay neighbours are asking the province to pause its review of two groundwater licence applications.

They want the science reviewed and their concerns heard before water decisions, that could impact their wells, are made.

“We’re dependent on residential wells for our water. We’re dependent on wells for our fire protection, we’re dependent on wells for our agriculture, and about five years ago these wells started to run dry in the summertime or run very low,” said Wendy Holm, chair of the Fanny Bay Groundwater Collective.

A decade ago the provincial government established the Water Sustainability Act that gives the government regulatory tools for protection, planning and enforcement for surface water and groundwater. At the time the government gave existing commercial groundwater users a temporary permit and now they’re working on license approval.

“If these licenses are approved these licenses are virtually forever,” said Holm.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

There are two companies — CERMAQ, a fish farming company, and Natural Glacier Waters, a water-bottling facility — that are working on getting theirs. The neighbours don’t know how much water CERMAQ’s application is for but they do know for Natural Glacier Waters.

“Absolutely shocked. The amount of water they are asking for is equal to the consumption of over 29,000 a day,” said Holm. Her group says the amount is 1,892,160 cubic metres a year or approximately 5.18 million litres of groundwater per day.

Now Holm, and the group she chairs that has 150 members so far, are asking the government to pause its license application reviews of the two companies.

“…and hold a public hearing so that we can look at the science, look at the amount of water that’s flowing into the aquifer, look at the risks of climate change,” said Holm.

In July, the government said no. The region’s MLA, Josie Osborne, says she’ll be bringing this issue up with the new minister as soon as she’s able.

“I expect government always to make decisions with the best science, the best evidence available and incorporating local knowledge and here’s where the voices of residents and others in the area, including First Nations, really need to be heard as so ensuring that the process accounts for that and ensuring that there’s an ability to revisit decisions as time wears on,” said Osborne.

In a statement, the government says ministry staff will consider factors such as how much water is used, when it is used, and what it is used for.

It goes on to say it’s accepting input from First Nations, stakeholders and the public.

Holm says the collective is now considering its legal options as it expects the commercial water licenses will be granted by June 2027 at the latest.

CHEK News reached out to CERMAQ and Natural Glacier Waters but has yet to get a response from either.

Dr. Sylvie Argouarch loved travelling, cycling, and spending time with her family. Her husband, Hugh Aitken, looks at a photo from their last trip together.

“This was one of our last major trips to Japan. And that was in Nikko, Japan. We tended to travel a lot,” Aitken said.

Argouarch, a psychiatrist, was cycling to appointments in Broadmead in July 2025 when she was struck and killed while riding through a marked crosswalk.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“Sylvie was an incredible person. Anything she took on, she took on with 110 per cent. And she has given my daughter and I a great deal of strength to get through the last 15 months,” Aitken said.

An SUV driven by Dugan Ian Ingram ran a red light and drove into Argouarch.

Charged under the Motor Vehicle Act for driving without due care and attention, Ingram received a two-year driving ban and $2,000 fine – the maximum penalties.

Three Victoria councillors – Dave Thompson, Jeremy Caradona and Jack Sandor – want to pass a motion that will result in more severe consequences for drivers like Ingram.

“At its heart, it’s a motion to try to improve the safety for Victoria residents. We’ve seen some really tragic incidents recently. And safety is required from all three levels of government: municipal, provincial and federal,” Thompson said.

The motion asks Mayor Marianne Alto to write to provincial and federal ministers, calling for tougher penalties for reckless drivers, including longer driving prohibitions, vehicle impoundments and higher fines, as well as the installation of more red-light cameras.

It also urges the federal government to consider pursuing dangerous driving causing death charges more frequently.

“The fact is, not to punish people with a good history of driving for one simple, small mistake. The point is to identify people who have clearly shown a pattern of being repeat offenders, of being dangerous drivers,” Sandor said.

Aitken says nothing will bring his wife back, but if new penalties prevent another family from going through the pain that his has, then he supports it.

“His sentence was a two-year driving prohibition and a $2,000 fine. And to me, those numbers just are staggering,” Aitken said.

In a statement to CHEK News, the Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General Jessy Sahota addressed the motion.

“Every death or serious injury on B.C.’s roads is a tragedy, and my thoughts are with the families and loved ones who have lost someone or whose lives have been changed by high-risk driving behaviours,” Sahota said.

“Our government remains committed to improving road safety and reducing serious injuries and fatalities through enforcement, education, engineering and partnerships with communities and law enforcement agencies across British Columbia.”

The minister says he has recently taken on the Public Safety and Solicitor General portfolio and is being briefed on several public safety matters, including road safety. He says he looks forward to hearing more about the concerns and working with partners to find ways to improve safety on B.C. roads.

The motion comes before Victoria city council on Thursday.

]]> 1363891 McGuinty says he can’t explain Pentagon’s criticism of Canada’s defence spending https://cheknews.ca/mcguinty-says-he-cant-explain-pentagons-criticism-of-canadas-defence-spending-1363892/ Tue, 24 Nov 2026 23:18:17 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363892

Defence Minister David McGuinty said Tuesday he can’t "divine" the thinking behind the Pentagon's recent criticism of Canada's defence spending — after the Trump administration took some symbolic steps to upend long-standing norms in North American continental security.

The post McGuinty says he can’t explain Pentagon’s criticism of Canada’s defence spending appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Defence Minister David McGuinty said Tuesday he can’t “divine” the thinking behind the Pentagon’s recent criticism of Canada’s defence spending — after the Trump administration took some symbolic steps to upend long-standing norms in North American continental security.

“The amount of co-operation that we are pursuing together under Norad has not changed. What we are doing together at NATO has not changed,” McGuinty told reporters in Ottawa. “Our military-to-military co-operation has not changed.”

Under U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon has undermined the long-standing bilateral defence relationship as Ottawa continues to review its plans for a fleet of American F-35 fighter jets.

Hegseth last week issued a classified memo imposing restrictions on military co-operation with Canada on think-tanks and socializing.

On Monday, the Pentagon released what it called a “fact sheet” which said Canada’s defence spending has limited the country’s ability to contribute to the protection of North America.

The Pentagon in May also paused the Permanent Joint Board on Defense, an advisory forum for U.S.-Canada bilateral defence co-operation that was established in 1940.

A senior U.S. Department of Defense official said the memo was intended to ensure a unified objective during engagements with Canada. It does not affect military operations.

The official from U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration briefed a small group of Canadian journalists Monday on background in order to speak more candidly about Canada-U.S. relations.

The official, who said the Pentagon is looking for Canada to commit to a realistic approach focused on military efficiency, cited the F-35 review. 

The Liberal government has yet to reach a decision on its order of F-35 fighter jets from Lockheed Martin and the purchase has been under review for more than a year.

The official claimed the Canadian Armed Forces sees the F-35 jets as superior to the alternatives but Ottawa is focusing on a middle-power strategy and prioritizing industrial policy and parochial trade issues over defence commitments.

Canada has long faced criticism over its lagging defence spending but Trump’s administration has connected it directly to larger trade issues, including the renewal of the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement on trade.

Earlier this year, Canada announced it would purchase early warning planes from Sweden’s Saab rather than Boeing.

Last March, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada had met for the first time the NATO requirement to spend the equivalent of two per cent of GDP on defence. The target was set in 2014 and Canada was among the NATO members which had never hit it.

When NATO members met last year in The Hague, they agreed to increase their defence spending to the equivalent of five per cent of GDP by 2035 — 3.5 per cent for core military and defence and 1.5 per cent for broader security and defence-adjacent investments that were loosely defined.

The U.S. official said it’s good to see Canada make “modest” progress on defence spending but accused Ottawa of not having a realistic plan for the new NATO benchmark.

The U.S. official said the gap between rhetoric and reality in Ottawa is the widest among the NATO partners. They also said Canada’s readiness under Norad is well below what is expected and the military organization doesn’t have proper investment from Ottawa.

The Pentagon is exploring how to protect the United States in the event it cannot rely on Canada to meet its obligations, the official added.

McGuinty was pressed by reporters on whether Canada would meet the five per cent commitment. He said Canada has a path to spending the equivalent of four per cent of GDP on defence by 2030.

When asked how the U.S. reacted to Canada’s four-per-cent plan, McGuinty’s response was terse.

“Canada is a sovereign nation,” he said. “I’ll be very direct. We don’t report to the United States.”

The recent federal budget charted a course to meeting the spending targets by 2030 but did not look at spending beyond that year. That plan includes spending 2.6 per cent of GDP, or about $99 billion, on core military, including ammunition and soldiers’ salaries.

“Canada has, for a long time, not lived up to our allies’ expectations,” said Jamie Tronnes of the Center for North American Prosperity and Security, a project of the Macdonald-Laurier Institute.

She added that should spur American and other allied militaries to double down on pushing Canada to increase its spending.

“A frozen relationship can only thaw with dialogue,” Tronnes said in an email.

“The (Department of Defense) strategy of disengagement in public forums says more about what the secretary of the (Department of Defense) is trying to impose on his own department, which is a one-voice-speaks-for-all policy, rather than the best way to engage with allies, especially those who may not like the messenger.”

]]>

The first meeting of the newly elected Saanich council came with a slew of notices of motion, including one to reduce the height of an in-progress affordable housing project and a pause on bike lane installations.

Saanich council was sworn in during a council meeting on Nov. 2, then had its first meeting to discuss issues on Nov. 23.

Coun. Matt McGeachie started things off with a notice of motion regarding an approved affordable housing project that is currently in the excavation phase.

“Whereas the final Nellie McClung Library redevelopment plan was approved without adequate public consultation, and whereas the University Heights Centre has buildings that do not exceed six stories, which serve as the maximum height from which other buildings should scale, and whereas the location of the building is outside of the 200-meter transit-oriented development area of the Shelbourne and McKenzie intersection,” McGeachie said when introducing the notice of motion.

“Therefore be it resolved that the District of Saanich engage with the Capital Regional Housing Corporation, the Province of B.C. and other potential stakeholders, with the aim of reducing the height of the Nellie McClung redevelopment project.”

Notices of motion in Saanich are when a member of council introduces a proposal to bring forward an idea or specific course of action to be discussed at a future council meeting. None of the notices of motion were discussed during the Nov. 23 meeting.

A date was not set to discuss the building height, but McGeachie noted “given that they’re digging a hole in the ground right now, the sooner we can consider that, the better.”

The project, which was formerly the site of the Nellie McClung Library and is now referred to as the Cedar Hill Library and Affordable Housing Development, was approved by Saanich in March 2025. Demolition then began in December 2025 and a building permit was issued in May 2026.

RELATED: Construction begins on 210-unit affordable housing tower, library in Saanich

It is an 18-storey mixed-use building with a library on two levels and 210 affordable rental homes above. There will also be a three-storey underground parkade.

The project has received a $34.6 million capital grant from the BC Community Housing Fund, and a commitment to the operating subsidy for a mix of rent levels. The total construction cost is estimated at $157.8 million.

Jeremy Caradonna, chair of the Capital Region Housing Corporation, says he cannot comment at this point as the motion has not yet been debated or passed by Saanich council.

“If the motion passes and comes to the CRHC, the Housing Corporation would likely respond with a formal, public letter to the District of Saanich, which would provide the perspective of the CRHC at that time,” Caradonna said in an email to CHEK News.

CHEK News has reached out to McGeachie, the Greater Victoria Public Library and the Ministry of Local Government, Housing, Sport and Culture for more information.

BC Housing said it is unable to comment due to restrictions based on the recent election.

Bike lane review and moratorium

McGeachie then introduced a second notice of motion, calling for staff to look at the bike lanes on Mann Avenue, with the goal of restoring parking.

“Whereas bike lanes were installed on Mann Avenue without proper public consultation, and whereas the District of Saanich removed all parking on the street, thereby overwhelming surrounding neighbourhoods with parked cars, and whereas the bike lanes remain underutilised,” McGeachie said.

“Therefore be it resolved that council direct staff to review the current bike lane configuration with the goal of restoring vehicle parking on Mann Avenue. Consideration should be given to utilising the Centennial Trail as a potential alternative to the present design.”

The Mann Avenue bike lanes were installed over summer 2026.

Saanich held two rounds of public engagement on the project.

“Thousands of residents were informed and engaged from 2016-2018 and 2022-2024 during the development of both plans through press releases, print ads, promotional cards, ads stamped on utility bills, social media, District website updates, workshops, and open house events,” an archived information page for the project says.

“After completion of the community engagement, the public was given the opportunity to provide further input when Staff presented the Plans to Council. Through that consultation municipal staff and our consultant were informed of desired routes and connections, and our proposed routes and connection were confirmed.”

Coun. Lorne DeLarge then introduced a notice of motion calling for a moratorium on bike lanes and other traffic calming.

“Council hereby places an immediate moratorium on the installation of any further bike lanes and traffic calming initiatives, including associated streetscape modifications, physical barriers, and signage throughout the District of Saanich, until further notice by resolution of this council,” DeLarge said when introducing the notice of motion.

“This moratorium shall not apply where a legally binding contract is already in place prior to the adoption of this resolution, or halting or cancelling work would result in financial, legal, or operational harm to the district, or failing to proceed with installation of or signage would create an immediate public safety concern.”

Traffic calming initiatives in Saanich follow a Road Safety Action Plan adopted in October 2024, which aims to achieve “Vision Zero.”

“Vision Zero is an ambitious goal to eliminate traffic fatalities and serious injuries on Saanich roads, while ensuring safe, healthy, and equitable mobility for all people,” an information page says.

“Vision Zero is a new paradigm for road safety. It recognizes that human error is inevitable and an integrated approach – called the Safe System Approach – is needed to improve the safety performance of our transportation network.”

To create the plan, Saanich underwent consultation which included a question about which changes would make people feel more comfortable travelling around Saanich.

Bike lanes were the top answer, followed by sidewalks, road improvements, enforcement and traffic calming.

Retractable leash changes

DeLarge also introduced a notice of motion to repeal the retractable leash ban.

“Council directs that the restriction on retractable leashes established under Animals Bylaw 2400 [sic] Amendment Bylaw 2023 Number 9924 be rescinded, and that retractable leashes be permitted for use in parks and public spaces throughout the District of Saanich,” DeLarge said.

“And staff be directed to prepare and bring forward for Council’s consideration an amending Bylaw specifically updating the definition of leash so that retractable leashes constitute a valid leash throughout the municipality.”

When the ban was being discussed, then-coun. Karen Harper said that retractable leashes are “generally dangerous to both people, pets, and the environment.”

READ PREVIOUS: Retractable leashes for dogs to soon be banned in Saanich after council decision

Engagement and economic development notices of motion

Mayor Rishi Sharma then introduced the final two notices of motion in the first meeting.

The first is to hold a town hall in January 2027 then further town halls held throughout 2027, and the second is to strengthen economic development in Saanich.

“Council direct staff to explore opportunities to strengthen economic development in Saanich, with a focus on business retention, expansion, investment attraction, entrepreneurship, and diversification of the municipal tax base, initiate discussions with the Greater Victoria Chamber of Commerce regarding the potential establishment of a satellite chamber office in Saanich, explore opportunities to establish a business accelerator hub, potentially in partnership with the chamber, to provide access to mentorship, networking, business advisory services, and other supports for entrepreneurs and existing business,” Sharma said.

“Identify potential partnerships with the University of Victoria, Camosun College, industry organisations, regional economic development partners and senior levels of government examine opportunities to utilise existing municipal or partner facilities, leverage external funding, and report additional cost to taxpayers, Make sure we are working with our Indigenous partners on any economic development opportunities, and report back to council.”

Motions to return to council at future date

Saanich’s bylaws require that notices of motion return to regular council meetings, but given the large number, council approved waiving the requirement to allow three to return to the special council meeting on Nov. 30.

The mayor and staff will determine which three should come before council on Nov. 30, with the rest to return for the regularly scheduled meeting on Dec. 7.

]]> 1363819 Fact File: Cruise line didn’t cite homelessness for decision to end Halifax stops https://cheknews.ca/fact-file-cruise-line-didnt-cite-homelessness-for-decision-to-end-halifax-stops-1363860/ Tue, 24 Nov 2026 22:10:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363860

A claim spread online last week that a cruise line's decision to cancel stops in Halifax resulted from passenger complaints about being confronted by people who were homeless.

The post Fact File: Cruise line didn’t cite homelessness for decision to end Halifax stops appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A claim spread online last week that a cruise line’s decision to cancel stops in Halifax resulted from passenger complaints about being confronted by people who were homeless. Online users cited a Daily Mail story about the cancellations that claimed passengers complained of encountering a “zombie apocalypse” in the port city.

Norwegian Cruise Line said its decision to add an extra night in Bermuda rather than sailing to the Nova Scotia capital was a response to “guest feedback,” but it never described the nature of the feedback. Norwegian continues to stop in Halifax on other cruise itineraries, as do other cruise operators, who say they have received positive feedback from passengers.

THE CLAIM

After the website Cruise Fever reported on Nov. 16 about the change to Norwegian Cruise Line’s Bermuda itinerary for next year, some people on X speculated that it was because passengers had unpleasant experiences in downtown Halifax.

In a post the next day on the Daily Mail’s X account, the newspaper linked to its reporter’s story about the cancellations. “Norwegian Cruise Lines axes 17 Nova Scotia trips as guests complain Halifax is now ‘zombie apocalypse’ hellscape filled with vagrants,” the post said.

In the story, the reporter drew a connection between the cruise line’s cancellation of the Halifax trips and the city’s homeless population. 

It included quotes from social media users described in the story as “travellers,” sharing their thoughts and experiences about the city. 

“I am sure it has nothing to do with the zombie apocalypse they stumble across when they find the downtown east side,” one person quoted in the story said. Many online users later repeated the term “zombie apocalypse” in their own posts on X, Instagram, and Facebook.   

“When tourists start choosing to avoid Canadian cities, it says something about the state of our country,” one user said in a post that had received over 120,000 views as of Nov. 23.

THE FACTS  

Before the change, the cruise line’s seven-night itinerary for the Norwegian Breakaway sailing from Boston included a stop in Halifax before heading to Bermuda. 

In an emailed statement, a Norwegian Cruise Line spokesperson said the decision to cancel the Halifax stop was in response to unspecified “guest feedback.”

The spokesperson said Bermuda schedules have been changed next year to give passengers “more time to explore the island.” The company’s Canada and New England cruises will continue to stop in Halifax in 2027 and 2028.

In a public Facebook group for people travelling with Norwegian Cruise Line, the change received mixed reactions: most welcomed the extra time in Bermuda but others were disappointed they wouldn’t visit Halifax. None of the commenters mentioned the city’s homeless population.

Other cruise operators that stop in Halifax said they have not heard complaints. “Our guests consistently share positive feedback about their time in the city,” said Andrea Zito, CEO of Swan Hellenic Cruises.

Mike Hicks, a spokesperson for Victory Cruise Lines, said Halifax is becoming increasingly popular among its passengers. “We are expanding our presence in Halifax with additional calls and the introduction of dedicated Halifax round-trip voyages,” he said. 

A search of quotes in the Daily Mail story reveals they were drawn from comments left by online users on the Cruise Fever post that first reported the itinerary change. That post referred to Norwegian cancelling visits to “a Canadian port of call.”

One example was a user who said she was based in British Columbia and wrote: “I am sure it has nothing to do with the zombie apocalypse they stumble across when they find the downtown east side.” While Halifax does not have a neighbourhood known as the downtown east side, Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside has a reputation for problems of homelessness and drug use.

Another user, who said he is from rural Saskatchewan and had recently visited Halifax on the cruise, did raise homelessness as an issue. “The touristy stops in Halifax were fine. If you got out and walked about downtown, the amount of street people was uncomfortable,” he said. “Oddly walking around downtown Boston actually felt safer.”

Other commenters quoted in the Daily Mail did not say they had been passengers on the Halifax cruise.

Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston denounced the Daily Mail story on his X account.

“Millions of visitors annually who come here to see all the wonderful things the city has to offer. I’m down enjoying the city’s waterfront often. This is a garbage story quoting random anonymous Twitter accounts to create a clickbait headline,” he said.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 24, 2026.

A former on-call teacher in the Nanaimo Ladysmith School District has been handed a lifetime ban on his licence after pleading guilty to a child sex abuse material charge.

Darrell Christopher Gilkes was an on-call teacher in the Nanaimo Ladysmith School District.

On June 23, 2023, the school district made a report to the commissioner that Gilkes had been arrested two days prior for possession and distribution of child pornography. At this time, Gilkes signed an undertaking to not teach in any role or permission needing a certificate or letter of permission.

The commissioner later launched an investigation into Gilkes on May 15, 2024, after learning that he was charged with possession and distribution of child pornography.

Two days earlier, Gilkes had been charged with transmitting, making available, distributing, selling, advertising, importing or exporting child pornography between Dec. 4, 2022 and June 21, 2023, and possessing child pornography in the same time period.

On June 26, 2024, the school district informed the commissioner that Gilkes’ employment had been terminated.

In October 2024, the Criminal Code was amended to change the terminology from child pornography to child sexual abuse and exploitation material.

Gilkes pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography on April 23, 2025, and on March 31, 2026, he was sentenced to one year in jail, followed by two years’ probation.

He was also given a DNA order, given five-year restrictions under section 161 of the Criminal Code, and ordered to comply with the Sex Offender Information Act for 20 years.

The BC Prosecution Service says a stay of proceedings was ordered for the charge for transmitting, making available, distributing, selling, advertising, importing or exporting child pornography.

The B.C. Commissioner for Teacher Regulation issued a lifetime ban from teaching in the kindergarten to Grade 12 system and independent schools because the offence erodes public confidence in the teaching profession and school system, and he failed to act ethically by violating the laws.
